On Monday, March 12, 2012 10:46:18 PM UTC-4, Ben Goodrich wrote:
We should cut out the loops since they are equivalent to

log_prob += log_sds.sum() * K * 2.0;

That was a mistake. It should be (and now is)

log_prob += (log_sds.sum() + log(2.0)) * K;

The whole thing may well be fixed as of commit 68c0587 . I also reparameterized wishart2x2.stan so that it matches the parameterization of wishart.stan and now they both yield the same output in --test-grad mode. However, the posterior means differ slightly from each other --- albeit more than I would expect from finite precision issues --- when you run them both for 2000 iterations starting with the same seed. So there may be some other bug lurking still.

Ben

On Monday, March 12, 2012 11:17:38 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
How are you even seeing W?  The test_grad function
only prints the unconstrained value.

I added a std::cout << "W = " << std::endl << W << std::endl;

to the C++ file temporarily.
Should I make the changes or do you want to?
I did before seeing this post.

1.  replace the two loops in read_cov_L() with:

     log_prob += log_sds.sum() * K * 2.0;

But I don't see why that's right.  If it's just the
diagonal, then isn't that just transforming var -> sd?
In which case I see the 2.0 * log_sds.sum(), but why
the K?

It wasn't quite right. The two Jacobians in question here are both diagonal. The first Jacobian is for the transformation from correlations to covariances (of order K choose 2). The derivative of a the i,j covariance with respect to the i,j correlation is sd_i * sd_j, and the product of each K choose 2 pairs of standard deviations goes on the diagonal. So, that log determinant is (K - 1) * log_sds.sum().

The second Jacobian is for the transformation from standard deviations to variances (of order K). The derivative of the ith variance is 2 * sd_i. So, the log determinant is (2.0 * sd).log().sum(), which is K * log(2.0) + sd.log().sum(). So, the correct line (which is in the code now) is

log_prob += (sds.log().sum() + log(2.0)) * K;
2.  Add the Jacobians back in for the cov_matrix_constrain()
Yes, that was necessary.
Now I have to go back and follow your unbranch instructions.
